Round 3 external comparisons (analysis package 1.4.0)

Read-only inputs
The SQLite snapshot, the Round 2 raw-response bundles and every archived baseline table are read without modification. FrozenBundles verifies archive and member SHA-256 hashes and reads selected members directly; it does not restore or change the Round 2 cache. The same 49,788 uniquely resolved DOI keys are reused. DOI resolution is not an adjudication of cited-study identity.

Publication-availability sensitivity
Earlier working-group acceptance cutoff dates are applied to OpenAlex publication-date proxies. Three date filters are separate comparisons: retain all valid dates, exclude January 1, and exclude day 1 of every month. A first-day value is treated as uncertain precision, rather than a proven imputation. Each exclusion changes the observed cohort and is not a correction to an unknown full-date truth. The DOI-matched cohort is defined within each report. Its common-source variant restricts both report sets to the same observed source support; it does not select the intersection of document IDs, which would force reuse to unity.

Age benchmark
The main external age comparison uses 30 inclusive annual bins: 1984–2013 and 1992–2021, or ages 0–29 from the annual cutoff origin. IPCC units are raw-reference occurrences and pool units are unique OpenAlex works. The older 1980-origin windows remain separate. Broad and narrow climate queries are both reported. The matched and unmatched occurrence cohorts partition the all-extracted cohort within every fixed window.

Outlet recovery and uncertainty scenarios
Unmatched occurrences use only their unique punctuation-repaired raw DOI; matched occurrences use the archived preferred DOI. Conflicting work resolutions remain ambiguous. The journal target requires OpenAlex work type article/review and primary source type journal. Unknown source or type is never silently relabelled journal. A single assigned ID may occur in matched and unmatched occurrence groups; these diagnostic groups cannot be added as if disjoint ID populations.
The allocation curve excludes positively known other types and retains unresolved type/source IDs as potentially journal. At alpha=0, unknown IDs follow known-source frequencies within five-year cited-year bins. IDs with several cited years use the earliest parsed cited-version year for this sensitivity only. Bins with no known support use report-wide known-source frequencies, and their number is reported. As alpha increases, the unknown mass shifts either toward the largest report source or toward one distinct source per unknown ID. These are fractional-assignment scenarios, not measured journal classifications or population confidence intervals.

New API acquisition
The installed literature_search_openalex skill CLI supplies fetch_with_retry and the polite_http transport. The wrapper adds environment-only credentials, exact transport-body capture before JSON parsing, UTC timestamps, parameter hashes, a local fee ceiling, and cursor pagination documented at https://help.openalex.org/api/grouping/. The CLI's command handler lacks cursor support, so the wrapper calls the CLI's own fetch function with the documented cursor parameter; it does not implement another HTTP transport. Successful 100-group prefixes are replayed exactly; future pages use the documented 200-group capacity. All group buckets including unknown are required to sum to the API total before a full-pool D2 can be computed. New acquisition totals are distinct from the immutable Round 2 totals.
An initial timeout had no response body and unknown billing. It is preserved as a failed request with a conservative local fee reservation. Following the user's explicit continuation authorization, each unchanged request may have at most two additional attempts; every failed attempt is archived separately. Non-transient HTTP failures stop. The fee ceiling includes observed successful charges and conservative failed-attempt reservations.

Relative risk and indirect comparator
A relative risk uses an exposure-stratified probability design with a complete query-defined AR5-cited exposure frame and a random sample from the non-exposed pool. The script selects an SRS of at most 500 exposed works and at most 1000 unexposed works before obtaining later-citation counts. Inverse inclusion probabilities are recorded. The outcome is membership in frozen DOI-resolved matched AR6 works, not all true IPCC citations. Publication-year/source-type Mantel–Haenszel risk ratios are distinct from odds ratios. A second stratification adds 2014–2021 citation-count bins (0, 1–9, 10–99, 100+), obtained by exact citing-work count queries rather than zero-filling absent rolling-year API fields. A 2500-draw exposure-stratified finite-population bootstrap describes sampling uncertainty. Conditioning on later citations is a selection sensitivity, not a causal adjustment. Unsupported strata and undefined bootstrap draws are counted.
The indirect comparator uses a separately seeded later-pool sample and the same frozen raw-DOI AR5 target works. Empty referenced_works lists remain a coverage uncertainty. The reported estimates use complete archived observations; missing required inputs stop estimation.

Acquisition stop and completed subset
An interim checkpoint preceded completion of the narrow AR6 source population and source-type/ISSN-L enrichment. The user canceled further model validation, while the other scientific analyses continued under the existing OpenAlex authorization. The separate completed_pool_v1 registry therefore uses only the two complete broad-query source-ID populations. It verifies the full archived cursor chain and excludes unknown-source works explicitly. Its windows are 1980–2013 and 1980–2021. Equal-size subsampling does not control unequal window lengths or missing-source coverage. It is a broader-source comparison, not a journal-only result or a selection effect. At that interim checkpoint, the complete journal/ISSN-L, relative-risk and random-pool indirect comparisons were unavailable. Subsequent complete registries are separate outputs.

Strict journal article/review source comparison
The separate journal_strict_v1 registry restricts both OpenAlex work type (article/review) and primary-source type (journal), then counts each assigned ID once per report. The matched-only and matched-plus-DOI-recovered-unmatched cohorts are separate comparisons. Repeated resolved mappings across occurrence statuses are collapsed; a conflicting work/source/type mapping stops the workflow. Source IDs define outlets. Independent multivariate-hypergeometric subsampling uses the smaller report cohort size,2000draws and seed20261011. Its percentiles describe equal-size composition sensitivity, not a population confidence interval or a linkage-accuracy interval. This strict filter is narrower than the immutable Round2 journal_sources filter, which restricted source type alone.

Final acquisition and support reporting
The completed acquisition contains2516successfulresponses and1500complete2014–2021citing-work count observations. These counts come from explicit citing-work publication-year queries, not zero-filled rolling counts_by_year fields. The risk frame consists of116220journalarticle/reviewquery works published1980–2013, including5304frozen AR5-cited and110916otherworks. Samples500/1000 carry fixed inverse-inclusion weights10.608/110.916. Source type is constantjournal, so the first comparison stratifies bypublicationyear; the second adds later-citation-countbins. Sample-supported strata and excluded sample/expanded masses are reported separately. Empty and missing outgoing-reference fields are distinguished in the indirect comparator. The same2664raw-DOIAR5targetworkIDs are used onbothsides.
